if.summary: Runs the block that follows only when the condition is true.

elif.summary: Another condition, tried only when the previous one was false.

else.summary: The block that runs when no earlier condition matched. Also the catch-all pattern in a match.

match.summary: Compares one value against a list of patterns and yields the first that fits.

loop.summary: One symbol for every loop: over a range, while a condition holds, a fixed number of times, or forever.

break.summary: Leaves the loop immediately. Add a label to leave an outer one.

continue.summary: Skips the rest of this pass and starts the next one.

lambda.summary: An anonymous function: parameters on the left, the expression it returns on the right.

return.summary: Hands a value back to whoever called the function.

pipe.summary: Feeds the value on the left into the function on the right.

arrow.summary: Separates a match pattern from its result, and renames a name in an import or export.

out.summary: Writes to the screen. It adds no line break of its own — that is what ¶ is for.

input.summary: Reads a line from the reader into a name, optionally showing a prompt first.

newline.summary: A line break in output. The pilcrow is typed with AltGr+R on most layouts.

newline_alt.summary: The same line break as ¶, for keyboards that cannot reach the pilcrow.

clear.summary: Erases the terminal and puts the cursor back at the top.

term_size.summary: Yields the height and width of the terminal, so a layout can fit itself to it.

out_pos.summary: Writes at an exact row and column instead of wherever the cursor was.

tui.summary: Takes over the whole terminal for the duration of the block, and restores it on the way out.

key.summary: Waits for a single keypress, without waiting for Enter.

key_nb.summary: Takes a keypress if one is ready and carries on immediately if not — how a game keeps moving.

sleep.summary: Pauses for the given number of milliseconds.

cli_args.summary: Collects the arguments the program was started with into a name.

assign.summary: Gives a name a value, and may give it a different one later.

const.summary: Gives a name a value once. Assigning to it again is an error the checker catches before the program runs.

incr.summary: Adds one to a number in place.

decr.summary: Subtracts one from a number in place.

compound.summary: Applies an operation to a name and stores the result back in it: += -= *= /= %= ^=.

hot.summary: Creates the name on first use with the neutral value for what is being done to it — zero for a sum, an empty collection for an append.

lifetime.summary: States that a name is finished with, so its memory can be released before the scope ends.

eq.summary: True when both sides are the same value.

neq.summary: True when the two sides differ.

lt.summary: True when the left side is smaller.

gt.summary: True when the left side is larger.

lte.summary: True when the left side is smaller or the two are the same.

gte.summary: True when the left side is larger or the two are the same.

and.summary: True only when both sides are true.

or.summary: True when at least one side is true. In a match pattern it separates alternatives.

not.summary: Turns true into false and false into true.

arith.summary: Add, subtract, multiply, divide, remainder and power: + - * / % ^.

len.summary: How many items a collection holds, or how many characters a text has.

append.summary: Yields the collection with one more item at the end.

insert.summary: Yields the collection with an item placed at the given position.

remove.summary: Yields the collection without the first item equal to the given value.

remove_all.summary: Yields the collection without any item equal to the given value.

remove_at.summary: Yields the collection without the item at that position, or without a whole range of them.

contains.summary: True when the collection holds that value.

find_all.summary: The positions of every item equal to the given value.

update.summary: Yields a new collection with one position replaced. The original is left alone.

replace.summary: Yields the text with every occurrence of one fragment swapped for another.

slice.summary: A run of items taken from a collection. Positions start at 1 and the end is included.

sort_by.summary: Sorts using a function that says which of two items comes first — how tuples get ordered by a field.

map.summary: Applies a function to every item and collects the results.

filter.summary: Keeps only the items for which the function is true.

reduce.summary: Folds a collection into a single value, starting from the given one.

split.summary: Cuts a text into pieces at every occurrence of a separator.

repeat.summary: A text joined to itself the given number of times — how rules and borders are drawn.

concat.summary: Appends to a text or a collection, accepting several values at once.

try.summary: Runs the block and, if something fails, hands control to the catch instead of stopping the program.

catch.summary: Handles a failure from the try above. Name an error type to handle only that kind.

finally.summary: Runs whether or not anything failed — where things get closed and cleaned up.

is_err.summary: True when the value is a failure rather than a result.

prop_err.summary: Returns the failure to the caller instead of dealing with it here.

err_type.summary: Names a kind of failure, so a catch handles that kind and lets others through.

num_eval.summary: Reads a number out of a text, in ASCII digits or any of 69 other scripts.

round.summary: Rounds to the given number of decimal places.

truncate.summary: Cuts to the given number of decimal places without rounding.

comma.summary: Formats a number with separators between groups of digits.

sci.summary: Formats a number as a mantissa and an exponent.

type_of.summary: Says what kind of value this is — Int, Float, Text, Bool, Array, Tuple.

to_float.summary: Converts a value to a decimal number.

to_int.summary: Converts to a whole number, rounding to the nearest.

to_int_tr.summary: Converts to a whole number by dropping the decimals. On a character, yields its code point.

typed_str.summary: Reads text and rejects anything longer than the stated limit, asking again.

typed_chr.summary: Reads exactly one character, asking again if given more.

base_lit.summary: A number written in hexadecimal, binary, octal or decimal: 0x 0b 0o 0d.

true.summary: The true value. Written as a symbol so it needs no word in any language.

false.summary: The false value. Written as a symbol so it needs no word in any language.

numerals.summary: Switches which digits numbers are written and printed in — Devanagari, Arabic-Indic, Thai and more. The pair of digits inside names the system by its own 0 and 9.

module.summary: Groups definitions under a name. The name has to match the file it lives in.

export.summary: Lists what a module offers to whoever imports it. Everything else stays private.

import.summary: Brings another module in under a local name.

mod_call.summary: Reaches a function or constant inside an imported module.

member.summary: Reaches a field of a named tuple.

shell.summary: Runs a command and yields its output as text.

script.summary: Runs another Zymbol file and yields its result. It is an expression, so its value has somewhere to go.

range.summary: Every value from the first to the last, both included.

brackets.summary: An array when they hold a list, an index when they follow one. Positions start at 1, and a negative one counts from the end.

braces.summary: Groups the statements that belong to a condition, a loop, a function or a module.

parens.summary: Group an expression, hold the arguments of a call, and build a tuple.

semi.summary: Separates several navigation paths inside one set of brackets, so one lookup can pull several values out of a nested structure.
